title: Radiomics random forest separates benign from premalignant polyps on CT colonography
summary: Polyps from a CT colonography screening trial were segmented and 1906 radiomic feature-filter combinations (shape, histogram, texture) were used to train a random forest on 107 polyps in 63 patients. In an external test set of 77 polyps in 59 patients it reached an AUC of 0.91 (95% CI 0.85 to 0.96), sensitivity 82% and specificity 85%, against a histopathology reference. The authors call it a proof-of-concept study with manual segmentation.
ai_technology: Random forest classifier on 1906 CT radiomics feature-filter combinations

evidence.tested: External test set of 77 polyps/59 patients with histopathology reference: AUC 0.91.
evidence.unknown: Small training set; manual segmentation; clinical utility untested; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest classified segmented polyps as benign or premalignant from image features.
